J.Dunsford (BELGRAVE) 29:30 (1st Youth); 22. R.Tanner (BELGRAVE) 31:11. MARCH 30th 1974 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - A.A.A. 10 Km.

As a result we are now relying on up and coming hopefuls including Richard Tanner. Apart from our 100% strength team, individually some excellent performances have been produced by Richard and John Hall.
Richard Tanner and Alan Lucas have both been consistant performers over the last few months and it is with regret that Alan has now returned to Australia.
Richard Tanner was fastest man in the LPR 9km at Blackheath Park on December 4th. He led the 34 strong field home in 44:24 with M.Scamell 5th in 46:09.
Dick Tanner and Ray Middleton were walking together in fourth place followed by a host of Surrey W.C. vests. Then came the rest of our team interspersed with more opposition vests.

Meanwhile Richard Tanner and John Hall were relentlessly pulling back the opposition to clinch their first National medals. Ray Middleton, having another of his worst races for a long time, was back again in the scoring team.

Ably led by Richard Tanner and Martin Lewin, we hope for some success next year despite some falling by the way-side before then. Although covered later by Gordon Doubleday a passing mention of the'Brighton' in this column is given to all the attendants who rose with the lark to travel the weary roa…
The Junior 3km event went to G.Morris of Steyning in 13:39.8 but filling 2nd and 3rd places were Martin Lewin (13:46.8) and Richard Tanner (13:55.2).
The trophy awarded by Surrey County for the best junior performance at the County Track Championships this year went to Richard Tanner for his win in the 3km Walk.

He easily won the Chippenham to Calne 6 mile road walk for the second successive year in another best time, almost 1½ minutes ahead of the 2nd man. With Richard Tanner 12th and Ray Middleton 14th the Bels retained the team race from Sarnia of Guernsey.

D.Cotton of Holloway Polytechnic won the Junior race over 5 miles in 36:38 with Richard Tanner our first man home in 9th spot with 39:14. Martin Lewin was close behind in 12th position with 39:41 with Tim Thorogood 13th in 39:56 and Steve Sharp 22nd 41:40.
Over £120 worth of beer was downed and the crowd ripped like locusts through the refreshments, supplied by CARL and BARBARA LAWTON and RICHARD TANNER.
Richard Tanner was 22nd in 22:52.0, Mike Scamell (Newham) 24th in 23:00.0 and Ray Middleton 27th in 23:25.0. As Ray approached the finish one of the crowd called out "You want another 50 miles, Ray!"

Three Belgravians competed in the City of London New Year's Day race over three miles, won by Leicester's B.Adams in 19:57.6. Fifth was Carl Lawton 20:53.6 with R.Tanner 22nd in 22:52 and R.Middleton 27th in 23:25.
In the Junior 8km at Chelmsford T.Thorogood placed 4th in 38:54, R.Tanner 5th in 39:19 and S.Sharp 18th in 44:54.
Richard Tanner placed 2nd in 44:31 and 6th was M.Scamell 46:05. Another 2nd place went to Richard six days later in the Cambridge H 10 miles race and he was timed at 82:15.
Soon to arrive was Richard Tanner who has established himself as a regular scorer in our teams. John Hall gave us another solid performance (it must be the Brighton air!).

One week later he took the Southern RWA '10' in 73:58 and again excellent backing from the rest of the team - Richard Tanner 3rd, Ray Middleton 5th and Tim Thorogood 6th - meant that the Bels won the team title.

We were not at full strength with a number of absentees and Richard Tanner competing in the 10,000m junior event. After the first of the five laps Roger Mills (Ilford) was leading Carl Lawton at a very fast pace.
In Rotterdam on the same day, Richard Tanner finished 3rd in a 3km event in 13:54.
In his first attempt at the event, Richard Tanner reached a praiseworthy 4th in the Police Barking to Southend Walk with 5hrs 13mins 17secs.
All police cadets they were:- George Nibre, Martin Lewin, Richard Tanner, Tim Thorogood, Terry Moore and Stuart Bennett. Q: In what other aspects of athletics have you been involved?

Richard Tanner had gone out fast at the start but paid for it later when John Hall swept past him. For a while there was some confusion over the times with Seatter being given 12:30.1 according to the electronic score-board but this was apparently caused by Mills strolling back and forth across the…

Nobody can walk a "Brighton" without the services of an attendant and our team was helped on its way by Carl and Barbara together with Dave's wife. Richard Tanner and Graham Seatter were in a "mini" and Tim Thorogood and Steve Sharp on cycles.

The team result was soon settled however with the arrival of Richard Tanner, who now walks with the authority of a seasoned competitor, closely followed by Shaun Maxwell to show us what a great addition he is going to be to our teams.
We sold over 800 books to make £207 profit - the second most in the country, and Richard Tanner sold a ticket that won £250. Get training for the 1977 100 x 1 mile relay on June 19th.
Richard Tanner recorded a personal best to complete the team. When the team placings were worked out Ilford AC took second medals and Belgrave and Brighton shared third place with equal scores.
Graham Morris of Steyning was the individual winner 30 seconds up on Richard Tanner's 25:05. Sixth was Jonathon Dunsford, 25:47, 11th Nigel Morris, 26:24, and 14th Stuart Bennett, 27:06.
Richard Tanner was the first man to retain a Club Championship in 1977 when he reached the 5 mile mark ahead of Jonathon Dunsford and thus kept his grip on the Junior "Olympic Cup".
One of our previous team, Richard Tanner, was missing as he was competing in the Police Barking to Southend walk the following day, this also affected other Clubs.
Carl again proved to be the winner, this time with 13:23, with Richard Tanner and Johnny Morris filling the other medal positions. Peter Morris took the Youths 2Km. in 11.08.
Following in are two faces of the past, double Olympian Eric Hall, beating the hour and Richard Tanner who has been off the scene for a couple of years.
In the annual Police Long Distance Walk, Barking to Southend on 16th May, Paul Blagg won in 4.49.31, 6.S.Marshall 5.53.49. 8.R.Tanner 5.59.59; 24.J.Morris 6.26.55; 31.R.Day 5.30.20.

Richard Tanner has almost returned to his standard of 7 years ago, not bad for someone who did not expect to take up walking again. John Newnham has not been at his best for a while but has still collected the odd team prize.
So it was left to Richard Tanner to not only bring home the team but to win overall with John Hall 2nd and Doug Fotheringham 5th. (The latter both did times faster than in the Belgrave).

In the W.A.A.A. 3Km Track Championship on 20th July Gail Porter placed 9th in 16:52.9. On the same day Richard Tanner won a 3Kms at Brighton in 13.05. Also Rachael Parrott was 19th in the W.A.A.A. 2½Kms in 14:34.9
